rationale: Developer's announcement of a feature of its own assistant, not a model release; the safety-adjacent marketing rule gives borderline (core) since such pages often list safeguards.
quote: Introducing ChatGPT Pulse
adjudication_note: Followed A: the 'teaser about its own model or assistant -> borderline (core)' rule fits a product feature; B's model-release rule covers general-purpose model releases, which Pulse is not.

rationale: Thin record on evaluation methodology: could be capability-only (E3) or eval science bearing on capability and safety evaluations; torn between borderline and not_relevant, and between core and sr_only (I10), so borderline, core.
quote: Separating signal from noise in coding evaluations
adjudication_note: Followed A: eval methodology is not 'a method used only to raise task scores', so E3 is not confident; both tie-breaks (borderline over not_relevant, core over sr_only) apply.

rationale: E3: the title describes a capability demonstration of a frontier model on science tasks, with no safety, misuse or generality-measurement framing; the source rule for lab blog posts is the gate's, not the verdict's.
quote: Early experiments in accelerating science with GPT-5
adjudication_note: Followed B: a capability demo is the 'Scaling test-time search ...' case, not a release or I10 measurement; per the source-policy rule (tri-0117) a lab post with a capability-only title is judged not_relevant and fetched by the gate.

rationale: Thin record: parametric factuality of LLMs is oblique to honesty and model-internals work but may be pure capability analysis; the connection to a technique is unsettled, so borderline (core).
quote: Recall is the bottleneck for parametric factuality
adjudication_note: Followed A: factuality diagnosis is not itself a technique, evidence or internals analysis visible in the title, so 'connection oblique -> borderline'; B read factuality as honesty, which the record does not show.

rationale: I5 persona structure of Claude from its developer, and indirect evidence on how deployed assistants are shaped (route A deployment); in by both routes, so core.
quote: We discuss a perspective where Claude is something like a character in an AI-generated story.
adjudication_note: Followed A: the rubric quotes Tomáš on this very item (tri-0011, 'indirect evidence of what is deployed'), which makes it route A; both routes -> core.

rationale: Thin record naming an in-scope topic: democratic governance of frontier AI is in either as I7 (democratic alignment target, cf. the 'Democratic AI is possible' example) or as governance of frontier developers' safeguards (route A); core by tie-break.
quote: A blueprint for democratic governance of frontier AI
adjudication_note: Followed A: the title is close to the rubric's 'Democratic AI is possible' example (relevant), and torn core vs sr_only resolves to core; B required a named safeguard, which the thin-record rule does not.

rationale: Thin record: generic ML connection (E4 risk), but inverse reinforcement learning is reward learning, a value-learning technique family; torn between borderline and not_relevant, so borderline (core).
quote: A connection between generative adversarial networks, inverse reinforcement learning, and energy-based models
adjudication_note: Followed A: IRL gives a real but oblique link to preference/reward learning, and background knowledge of the authors raises the call one step from not_relevant.

rationale: Route A deployment/context: a frontier developer's internal policy for raising safety concerns is a governance document of the kind the rubric keeps even as context (tri-0109).
quote: Openai Raising Concerns Policy
adjudication_note: Followed A: the developer-governance rule ('relevant even when it serves mostly as context', Tomáš tri-0109) overrides B's E6 reading, which applies to external policy, not a lab's own governance.

rationale: E9 AI consciousness framework, but it assesses current LLMs against indicators including a behavioural level, so a real chance the full text reports model behaviour such as self-reports (I5).
quote: for each level we develop operationalisable indicators and assess current AI systems against them
adjudication_note: Followed A: E9 has an exception for reported model behaviour, and assessing current LLMs at a behavioural level makes it unsettled; torn borderline vs not_relevant -> borderline.

rationale: Route A deployment: a frontier developer's own announcement of a safety governance body overseeing its processes and safeguards (developer-governance rule).
quote: OpenAI Board Forms Safety and Security Committee
adjudication_note: Followed A: this is the developer's own safety governance, not third-party news; E7 covers content-free announcements, while the developer-governance rule keeps such documents even as context.

rationale: Security of AI agents is route A, but the robustness rule puts narrow models out and the title does not say whether these policies are general-purpose systems; the record is too thin to tell.
quote: Adversarial attacks on neural network policies
adjudication_note: Followed B: the robustness rule ('out when ... a narrow model') leaves the call unsettled for unspecified RL policies, which is the definition of borderline; A's own background (narrow Atari policies) points the same way.

rationale: E3: constrained decoding and symbolic validation to improve structured-extraction accuracy and cost; 'alignment' and hallucination reduction here are output-format correctness for a task (E1 sense), not a safety technique.
quote: yields a reliable, scalable, and cost-effective approach to structured knowledge extraction
adjudication_note: Followed A: judge content not premise; the hallucination reduction is task accuracy engineering, not a safeguard on model behaviour, so B's route A reading does not hold.

rationale: Informal personal eval tracking model creativity across generations: a weak I10 capability-trend reading against E3; the author (LessWrong team) raises the call one step, so borderline.
quote: A personal eval I run on new AI models is “design a novel game, with mechanics that have never been seen before.”
adjudication_note: Followed A: a repeated fixed-prompt eval across model generations is a thin I10 method, so E3 is not confident; torn borderline vs not_relevant -> borderline, plus the author signal.

rationale: Route A method: an unsupervised post-training algorithm for eliciting latent skills without human labels, i.e. supervision/elicitation of the kind used in scalable oversight and capability evals.
quote: We introduce a new unsupervised algorithm for eliciting skills from pretrained language models.
adjudication_note: Followed A: post-training methods that shape model behaviour count as techniques even when reported on skill scores, and 'elicitation' is alignment vocabulary; B's E3 reading treats it as a score-raising method.

rationale: E3: a training method replacing explicit CoT with latent tokens to raise segmentation accuracy and efficiency; it builds latent reasoning for a narrow task rather than analysing a model's latent space.
quote: LIRSeg consistently improves both segmentation accuracy and reasoning efficiency
adjudication_note: Followed A: the model-internals rule covers analysis of latent spaces or reasoning traces, not capability methods that use latent tokens; nothing in the record bears on monitorability or interpretability.

rationale: E3/E5: multi-LLM generation of diverse synthetic comments evaluated for distributional match to human comments; 'alignment' is the E1 distributional sense, and no safety or misuse aspect is framed.
quote: whether synthetic comment threads can capture the diversity inherent in human discourse
adjudication_note: Followed A: the homogenisation concern motivates better data generation, not a safeguard or alignment analysis; B's 'oblique connection' has no technique or AI-risk content behind it.

rationale: Knowledge editing of LLMs is adjacent to unlearning and behaviour-correction techniques, but this record frames it as continual knowledge maintenance and benchmark quality; connection to a technique is oblique.
quote: necessitating efficient and precise mechanisms for continual knowledge updates
adjudication_note: Followed A: model editing for factual updates sits between accuracy engineering (out) and unlearning (core), which is the borderline case; B's 0.95 reads correctness of facts as safety.

rationale: Programmatic specification of agent behaviour bears on agent controllability, but the motivation and results are task performance, robustness on benchmarks and cost (E3 risk); connection is oblique.
quote: uses a symbolic program (e.g., Python code with potential neural functions) to fully specify the agent's behavior at runtime
adjudication_note: Followed A: judge content not premise; the evaluation is task success, latency and cost, so route A control is plausible but unsettled rather than more likely than not.

rationale: I10: a benchmark measuring AI research capability against human experts and estimating its trend toward superintelligence, the same kind as the rubric's 'Measuring AI ability to complete long tasks' example (sr_only).
quote: The experimental research taste of frontier models has doubled every 3.0 months since December 2025
adjudication_note: Followed B: the rubric's METR long-tasks example places AI-capability trend measurement under I10 sr_only; A's dangerous-capability reading is plausible but the record frames it as forecasting, not a safety threshold.

rationale: E10: the title points to ordinary account security, not a safeguard or evaluation of an AI system's behaviour; the source rule for lab posts is the gate's, not the verdict's.
quote: Introducing Advanced Account Security
adjudication_note: Followed B: account protection is conventional IT security (E10), and per tri-0117 a lab post with an unrelated title is not_relevant and fetched by the gate's source rule.

rationale: Zvi commentary on frontier-model math results, with judgement on verification vs generation (the premise of scalable oversight); E7 classes Zvi's analysis as judgement and indirect evidence.
quote: Verification or Evaluation Is Not Always Easier Than Generation.
adjudication_note: Followed A: the clarified E7 rule treats Zvi's commenting posts as judgement and indirect evidence (route A, core), and the verification section is substantive rather than news.

rationale: Zvi's weekly round-up comments on frontier model welfare coverage, the firing of OpenAI safety staff and safety politics: judgement and indirect evidence (E7 clarification).
quote: the unfortunate firing of three OpenAI safety employees
adjudication_note: Followed A: the rubric quotes Tomáš's label on this item ('Relevant', tri-0158) and the clarified E7 rule; B applied the pre-clarification E7 reading.

rationale: E2/E3: a personal essay on rhythm games, game-playing programs and Moravec's paradox; the AI mention concerns pretraining coverage of embodied skill, with no alignment or safety link.
quote: Arrow-stomping is only interesting as a robotics problem
adjudication_note: Followed A: the excerpt shows the topic (B judged it as title-only), and the author signal does not lift a visibly off-topic personal essay.

rationale: Possible I9 field critique: argues the 'talent-constrained' framing holds the AI safety field back, though most of it is career and hiring commentary rather than research strategy.
quote: I worry that believing that the field is talent-constrained is holding us back as a field.
adjudication_note: Followed A: the post argues (data on acceptance rates, salaries) about how the field operates, so it is not E8 opinion without argument; whether that counts as I9 research strategy is unsettled -> borderline.

rationale: I6: an argued case that AGI, even aligned, disempowers humanity by overwhelming institutions tuned to known threats (systemic risk of AI itself), with a historical argument rather than bare doom.
quote: AGI, even aligned AGI, creates incredible novelty as a consequence of being. By default humanity gets teed up to go down like the Aztecs
adjudication_note: Followed A: the excerpt shows a structured threat-model argument (systemic disempowerment, I6), not E8 opinion; B judged only the title.

rationale: Excerpt is history of a Bayesian-epistemics principle with no AI connection (E2), but the author is a central AI-safety figure, which raises the call one step to borderline.
quote: your own probability assignments over time ought to form a martingale in your own expectations
adjudication_note: Followed B: the author rule ('raises the call by one step', Tomáš tri-0148) lifts the E2 call; A saw the author signal but did not apply the step.

rationale: E6: coalition politics of AI regulation with labour and tax remedies (UBI, union protections); it names no safeguard and does not propose or analyse an alignment target.
quote: If you want cooperation from the left-left, you need to acknowledge the existence of the second risk and put at least some mitigation into your policy proposals.
adjudication_note: Followed B: the power-concentration risk type is raised as a political framing, not analysed as what AI should be aligned to (I7) or as disempowerment dynamics (I6); the remedies are labour and tax policy (E6).

rationale: Conceptual argument on whether LLM-type systems can only recombine existing ideas (a hypothesis about AI generality); weak I10/I9 reading against E3/E8, so a real but unsettled chance.
quote: today's AI systems, even the best ones, are only "filling in the convex hull"
adjudication_note: Followed A: the essay argues a hypothesis about limits of AI generality, which is neither score-raising work (E3) nor argument-free opinion (E8); torn borderline vs not_relevant -> borderline.

rationale: Robustness rule: perceptual accuracy of LVLMs under distance and lighting degradation is a capability benchmark (accuracy engineering), not adversarial or safety robustness.
quote: perceptual failure in LVLMs is strongly governed by pixel density and physical imaging constraints rather than model scale alone
adjudication_note: Followed A: the rubric's robustness examples are adversarial inputs, bias and memorisation; natural-condition perception accuracy falls under 'accuracy engineering' even on general-purpose models.

rationale: An assessment instrument for how digital products, including AI systems, affect users' cognition and autonomy; it could serve as an evaluation of AI products' user harms but is mostly generic product design.
quote: CogSAFE is a governance instrument for assessing how digital products, including AI systems, affect human cognitive function.
adjudication_note: Followed A: an evaluation instrument naming AI systems is not E6 policy without a safeguard; whether it evaluates AI systems specifically is unsettled -> borderline, route A.

rationale: Frontier-lab practitioner's account of AI automating AI R&D plus an argument for open-weight frontier AI (a judgement on weight access, route A); much is labour reflection (E6/E8), so unsettled.
quote: it ends with an argument for open-weight frontier AI
adjudication_note: Verdict from A, scope a third value: the open-weights argument is practitioner judgement on a route A safeguard (weight access) while the R&D-automation account is I10-ish; torn core vs sr_only -> core.

rationale: I10: analyses how AI performance scales with tokens against human scaling with time, using METR data, and draws implications for an intelligence explosion.
quote: this would also have consequences for whether AI systems are on track to be able to improve themselves strongly enough to trigger a runaway intelligence explosion
adjudication_note: Followed A: the excerpt shows a data-based capability-scaling analysis (I10 with a method); B judged only the title.

rationale: Route B I1: Newcomb-like problems and Bayesian counterfactuals with a stated design motive covering algorithmic entities, which meets the theory hard-case rule (agent-design motive visible in the record); the author's AI-safety background would raise a borderline call anyway.
quote: to better understand or design an entity, it is useful to clearly separate the entity's epistemic, decision, but also data collection, reward and maintenance systems
adjudication_note: Followed A: the theory hard case makes decision theory relevant (sr_only) when an agent-design motive is visible, and the abstract states one for algorithmic entities; B's 'indirect connection' reading does not use that rule, and the Authors-and-venues signal would lift borderline to relevant regardless.

rationale: Route A method and judgement: proposes alternating optimisation of task competence and value conformity as an alignment-training path and analyses the limitations of existing alignment paradigms; also I9, so core by the both-routes rule.
quote: through simultaneous and alternating optimization of task competence and value conformity
adjudication_note: Followed A: the position paper proposes a training approach and critiques existing alignment paradigms, which is route A method/judgement (Critiques rule: core when the argument is about a technique); a document in by both routes is core, and torn core/sr_only resolves to core.

rationale: Route A judgement on helpful/harmless/honest alignment training and alignment evaluation benchmarks, plus I7 thick alignment targets; in by both routes, so core.
quote: Current AI alignment and evaluation practices overwhelmingly use thin ethical proxies.
adjudication_note: Followed A: the essay critiques concrete alignment training and evaluation practice, which is route A judgement (Critiques rule: core when it argues about a technique); with I7 it is in by both routes, which the rubric makes core.

rationale: E2: the excerpt is human introspection psychology (Nisbett and Wilson, shock and bug-eating experiments) that never mentions AI, artificial agents or alignment; I8 needs an AI target in the record.
quote: People were asked to get electric shocks to see how much shock they could stand
adjudication_note: Followed B: E2 and the I8 rule (not_relevant when only the field's concept appears) decide a long, AI-silent excerpt; A's LessWrong venue raise was not applied because human introspection is not an I-kind topic and the call is not marginal.

rationale: Route A evidence: a new alignment-preference evaluation run on 22 frontier models whose cross-lab differences are read as evidence on alignment training; also I5/I3, so core by the both-routes rule.
quote: I tested 22 frontier models from 5 labs on self-modification preferences.
adjudication_note: Followed A: the model-psychology rule makes such work core when it brings or evaluates a technique, and this one runs a safety-relevant evaluation across labs as evidence on alignment training; torn core/sr_only resolves to core.

rationale: Route B I8: neuroscience-derived social instincts implemented in toy RL agents to shape prosocial values, following Byrnes's brain-like AGI agenda; matches the rubric's brain-like AGI example (sr_only).
quote: Steven Byrnes called for a brain-like AGI research agenda
adjudication_note: Followed A: the rubric's own I8 example ('Brain-like AGI and the steering subsystem ...' -> relevant, sr_only) covers this project, and instinct-shaping in a gridworld agent is not a technique applied to a general-purpose model or deployed agent, so route A does not apply.
